svg.text: The trip of one request out of a VPC
…and how to tell whether a NAT gateway is actually being used
AZ us-east-1a · one or more datacenters (×3: 1a / 1b / 1c each repeat this)
"public" only because its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW
every byte through it is counted
2,048 IPs − 5 reserved = 2,043 usable · every card (ENI) takes one
WORKLOADS · START trips → these use the NAT
PLUMBING / RECEIVERS · never start a trip → never use the NAT
Reading a card in EC2 → Network interfaces
Type not "Elastic network interface" or "lambda" → AWS plumbing
"Elastic network interface" → read Description / Instance ID:
i-… = EC2 · "AWS Lambda VPC ENI-…" = Lambda · "arn:aws:ecs…" = ECS
A workload card → find who deployed it and ask
ROUTE TABLES · live at VPC level
each subnet uses exactly 1 · one table can serve many
most specific match wins (most fixed bits)
VPC level · no card · free · S3 traffic skips the NAT
Deleting a NAT leaves its 0.0.0.0/0 row
as a blackhole (remove it) and keeps the
EIP (release it). Other rows keep working.
reply comes back the same way:
IGW → NAT swaps address back → EC2
OUTSIDE THE VPC · where the other rows of private-1a lead
TGW hub → other company VPCs, offices
Peering → partner VPC (exactly one VPC, not transitive)
How a route matches: /N = the first N bits must match
140… starts with bit 1; every 10.x route needs 0 → only /0 can match
Inside the NAT: rewrite the envelope, remember it
The private IP never appears on the internet: nobody outside can even name it.
Is this NAT used? Three checks in the AWS console
• Set Period = 1 day to see 15 months
• All zero → nobody walked through the door
• Resource map shows Name tags, not IDs
• Only plumbing cards → nothing can use it
• Workload card → find its owner, check it
busy VPC? trace route → subnet → cards
Under the hood: none of this is physical
A Nitro card on each AWS host checks routes + SGs
per packet; a mapping service knows where each
private IP really lives. You edit config (control
plane), the cards enforce it (data plane).
